conversation.content: Let's start a deployment record for the payments API.
[{"op": "add", "path": "/deployment", "value": {"app_name": "payments-api"}}]
Put the main application into its pod as the first running process.
[{"op": "add", "path": "/deployment/pod", "value": {"containers": [{"name": "app"}]}}]
Give that app a modest CPU reservation.
[{"op": "add", "path": "/deployment/pod/containers/0/cpu_request", "value": "500m"}]
Set a reasonable memory reservation for the app too.
[{"op": "add", "path": "/deployment/pod/containers/0/memory_request", "value": "512Mi"}]
Expose the app on its usual web traffic port.
[{"op": "add", "path": "/deployment/pod/containers/0/port", "value": 8080}]
Add a log shipping helper alongside the app.
[{"op": "add", "path": "/deployment/pod/containers/-", "value": {"name": "log-shipper"}}]
Keep the log helper lightweight on CPU.
[{"op": "add", "path": "/deployment/pod/containers/1/cpu_request", "value": "100m"}]
Give the log helper a small memory reservation.
[{"op": "add", "path": "/deployment/pod/containers/1/memory_request", "value": "128Mi"}]
Have the log helper listen on its internal metrics endpoint.
[{"op": "add", "path": "/deployment/pod/containers/1/port", "value": 24224}]
Add a request tracing helper to run alongside the other processes.
[{"op": "add", "path": "/deployment/pod/containers/-", "value": {"name": "trace-agent"}}]
Reserve a little CPU for the tracing helper.
[{"op": "add", "path": "/deployment/pod/containers/2/cpu_request", "value": "150m"}]
Give the tracing helper enough memory to buffer spans safely.
[{"op": "add", "path": "/deployment/pod/containers/2/memory_request", "value": "256Mi"}]
Have the tracing helper receive spans on the standard collector port.
[{"op": "add", "path": "/deployment/pod/containers/2/port", "value": 9411}]
Now note how many processes are running in that pod.
[{"op": "add", "path": "/deployment/pod/container_count", "value": 3}]
Add up the CPU reservations across everything in the pod.
[{"op": "add", "path": "/deployment/pod/total_cpu", "value": "750m"}]
Add up the memory reservations across everything in the pod as well.
[{"op": "add", "path": "/deployment/pod/total_memory", "value": "896Mi"}]
List the ports that will be reachable from the pod.
[{"op": "add", "path": "/deployment/pod/exposed_port_list", "value": [8080, 24224, 9411]}]
Place this deployment in the production payments area.
[{"op": "add", "path": "/deployment/namespace", "value": "prod-payments"}]
Tag it with the team that owns the service.
[{"op": "add", "path": "/deployment/owner_team", "value": "payments-platform"}]
Use a cautious rolling rollout for releases, with a little extra capacity and no planned downtime.
[{"op": "add", "path": "/deployment/strategy", "value": {"type": "RollingUpdate", "max_surge": "25%", "max_unavailable": "0"}}]
Record where this production rollout will run: the east coast region, its primary zone, and the shared production cluster.
[{"op": "add", "path": "/deployment/placement", "value": {"region": "us-east-1", "zone": "us-east-1a", "cluster": "prod-shared-01"}}]
Run four copies of this service for normal production traffic.
[{"op": "add", "path": "/deployment/replicas", "value": 4}]
Pin the service to the approved release image and only pull it when it isn’t already cached.
[{"op": "add", "path": "/deployment/image", "value": {"repository": "registry.example.com/payments/payments-api", "tag": "2026.06.1", "pull_policy": "IfNotPresent"}}]
Add the basic health check routes and give the process half a minute to settle before startup checks matter.
[{"op": "add", "path": "/deployment/health_checks", "value": {"readiness_path": "/ready", "liveness_path": "/live", "startup_grace_seconds": 30}}]
Mark the service as externally reachable over encrypted traffic through the standard public entry point.
[{"op": "add", "path": "/deployment/service", "value": {"type": "LoadBalancer", "protocol": "HTTPS", "external_port": 443}}]
Allow it to scale up during payment spikes, but keep a small floor in place.
[{"op": "add", "path": "/deployment/autoscaling", "value": {"enabled": true, "min_replicas": 4, "max_replicas": 10}}]
Add the runtime settings for production mode, the card provider, and normal logging verbosity.
[{"op": "add", "path": "/deployment/runtime_config", "value": {"environment": "production", "payment_provider": "stripe", "log_level": "info"}}]
Lock down the runtime so it uses a non-root account and cannot gain extra privileges.
[{"op": "add", "path": "/deployment/security_context", "value": {"run_as_non_root": true, "run_as_user": 10001, "allow_privilege_escalation": false}}]
Have Prometheus collect metrics from this service every 30 seconds.
[{"op": "add", "path": "/deployment/monitoring", "value": {"prometheus_scrape": true, "scrape_interval_seconds": 30}}]
Add the on-call contact and the regular Sunday maintenance slot.
[{"op": "add", "path": "/deployment/operations", "value": {"on_call_contact": "payments-primary", "maintenance_window": "Sun 02:00-03:00 UTC"}}]

edit_instruction: Remove the log-shipper sidecar from the pod.
conversation_pattern: Center the artifact on a pod with several containers, each with a name, a CPU request, a memory request, and an exposed port, where the pod's container_count, total_cpu, total_memory (stated sums over the containers), and exposed_port_list aggregate over the included containers. Around this core, add the realistic, independent details a deployment record would carry that do not depend on the container list, and vary the number of containers from sample to sample.
edit_pattern: Remove one specific sidecar container from the pod.
cascade_pattern: Removing the container deletes it from the container list, lowers container_count, removes its port from exposed_port_list, and re-derives total_cpu and total_memory as the stated sums over the remaining containers. Unrelated deployment metadata stays unchanged.
annotation_notes: remove log-shipper sidecar; container_count 3->2, total_cpu 750m->650m, total_memory 896Mi->768Mi, exposed_port_list drops 24224. | REVIEW EDIT (with author): exposed_port_list re-expressed as a per-element remove op (whole-array replace not expanded by leaf-level scorer -> phantom over+miss even for a perfect model).
